title: Emberbrook — the town-wide dressing pass
subtitle: The finishing window. The fixture levels are measured rather than guessed, the plaza is emitted as blocks a second camera can own, Festival Square has the market row the cut sits on, the stranded pad is gone and the seclusion stamp is re-earned against the ridge instead of the shoulder. Every frame is derived: no camera was aimed by eye and no placement was nudged. Both halves of every pair are the SAME camera — the before-pass is rendered through the dressed run's own solve, because a wipe between two solves is a lie with a slider on it.

sections.title: The districts
sections.blurb: One eye-level frame per **map parcel** — the same parcels that derive every scene contract and sceneKey, so the district set is the map's and not this lane's. The camera stands ON THE WALK NETWORK (a district frame is a place the player can be), at the standoff the target's own built extent solves for, at the lens and the min/max distances `emberbrook.cameras.json` already ratifies. Among the candidate stands the best nine-ray clear fraction on the target wins; a frame under 60% is REPORTED occluded, not fixed by moving the town.

sections.title: Before / after, from the same camera
sections.blurb: `--nodress` runs the identical derivation with every dressing stage skipped: same map, same harvest, same light key, same lens, same pixel grid. **And the same camera, which took a second run to be true.** The solver picks its stand by censusing the scene for occluders, and a scene with the dressing removed has different ones — measured, 6 of these 10 cameras MOVED between the two builds, `district-square` by 42 m. Six of the pairs below would have shown a camera move and invited you to read it as the dressing. The dressed run's cameras are now written to `town.cameras.json` and the before-pass renders through them verbatim: **10 of 10 reproduced to 0.1 m.** Drag the handle; the only thing that changes is the thing being reviewed.

sections.title: The fixtures, measured
sections.blurb: The bar was zero clipped pixels on the glass. `tools/emb_lum.py` grew a `clip` column for it — the share of pixels with ANY CHANNEL at 254+, measured per channel because a warm emitter pins R long before its luminance nears white — and a `--boxes` mode that says whether a measurement box laps a neighbouring object, because this lane got that wrong three times in the same twelve pixels.

rows.text: 7.0 — the blockout's own level, and the defect

rows: 1.6 — the previous round's first guess
sections.note: THE HARD BAR IS MET AT EVERY SWEPT LEVEL and only the blockout's 7.0 fails, which is the finding: the lantern never needed to be dim, it needed to stop being 7.0. sd RISES across the band (55.5 to 81.6), so inside it a brighter lantern carries MORE form — what a surface that has stopped clipping does. One lamp settles all fourteen: an emissive surface's radiance does not fall off with range. Box 524,265-572,312 on emb_lamp_00_road-gate_glass at 42.7 m in district-entrance.

sections.title: What the frames ask you to rule on
sections.blurb: The things these frames show that this lane did NOT decide, in the order they cost the most.

rows.text: THE HEARTLIGHT'S FLAME STILL CLIPS AT ITS FOOT, and three fixes have been refused by measurement.

rows: The flame BODY reads peak 216 with **0.00% clipped**; the 12-pixel band at its foot reads **33.85%**. Ablated: removing the ember bed changes that band BIT-IDENTICALLY, and removing the brightest single shell moves its mean by 3.4 — so no one component is responsible and the sum through the stack's common base is the mechanism. Staggering the shell bases was then swept and made it MONOTONICALLY WORSE (33.85 / 36.11 / 37.67), because nested shells are crossed by the same rays whatever their vertical offset: it relocates brightness, it does not reduce a sum.

coordinator's. A sum of emission terms has two levers — fewer terms or smaller terms. The body's headroom is the number that makes it tractable: only the foot fails. Compressing the ladder's top end (the innermost shell is 2.60x) reduces the sum through the deepest part without touching the outer shell that draws the silhouette.

rows.text: A --nodress frame is BLACK, and it is pre-existing.

rows: `town-nodress-district-gatefield.png` measures 0.0% non-black. The file it replaced was the same 256242 bytes and equally black, so nothing in this window caused it — but the pair below presents a black rectangle as a 'before', which is not a comparison. The DRESSED gatefield beside it is a normal frame (L=91.1, 0.00% clipped).
coordinator's — it is specific to the undressed build of that one camera, and it has been wrong for at least two rounds without anyone noticing.

rows.text: The market row is in the MAP now, not in the dressed blend.

rows: Stamp e4cbd13, searched then ratified: six stalls on a 150-degree axis with a 5.8 m THRESHOLD HOLE at (66.00, 47.46). The hole is the point — seam-canon 4 says a cut sits on a threshold and never mid-span of open floor. The blockout emits the massing (so it reaches the walk bundle, cine_regions and GateGrid), the dressing renders the record, and the plaza cut 2211 to 1862 cells around it.
nobody — this one is done, and the cameras lane can execute the split against it.

rows.text: The enclosure re-print went 13/16 to 15/16 and that is NOT the room getting better.

rows: 15 of 16 sectors close on a roofline or canopy, 11 at eye level, median eye-landing 15.0 m (was 18.4). The row is built massing inside the 25 m sweep, so the probe lands on it. The room's walls have not moved a metre — it is furniture registering as enclosure.

sections.note: This lane closed the fixture levels, the plaza blocks, the island pad, the seclusion regression, the crown gate and the market row this window. It did not touch the lighting grade, and it retracted two of its own findings (the Heartlight's stone, and a view-dependence that was a box artifact) rather than leave them standing.

sections.title: What the town broke, and what it cost
sections.blurb: Five failure classes the pilot could not have found at 30 m. Each was fixed in the RULE, never in the output, and each row carries the instrument that named it.
rows: `RR = 1e9` was a sentinel, and three rules spend it as a **length**
`dress_bank_planting` drew 260 candidates from a square of side 2xRR about the region centre, then kept the ones within 3.40 m of water
town-wide: **0 plants**, reported as success. Same code at the mill: 176

the region is the map's own landmark extent (centre 64.0, 56.0, radius 104 m); candidates are drawn around **each water body's own bounds**. Town-wide now **1112 plants from 1298 candidates, 86% accepted**
700 clumps/m2 is a density, and over a valley it is also a budget
one particle system for the whole request. Blender's `distribute_particles` sorts it in a **single-threaded** `BLI_qsort_r`
**2256 of 2257** stack samples inside nested qsort frames, 11 GB resident, **no output in 15 minutes**. 39,237 m2 x 700 = **27.5M particles**

the scatter is spent inside a **14 m band about the walk network** (9,546 of 39,237 m2 = 24.3%) because the plates are composed on the lanes; the request is tiled at 400k per system with crc-derived per-slab seeds. **6.68M over 17 slabs**, density unchanged
the ground oracle went through the **depsgraph**
`raycast_ground` called `Object.ray_cast`, which needs the EVALUATED mesh — and every `veg()` call creates an object, which TAGS the depsgraph. One realize of every instance so far, per placement

`execute_realize_mesh_tasks` + `adapt_mesh_domain_face_to_point` + `threaded_copy` at **100% of samples for over an hour**, part way through placements. It never looked like a hang because it was never idle

a standalone `BVHTree` over the ground's world-space verts, rebuilt only by the two stages that cut it. **No depsgraph in the oracle at all.** The same build reached bank planting and groundcover in minutes
the shot **solver** paid for the scatter on every ray
the build finished and the solver hung, which looks identical from outside. Each candidate stand costs one ground ray and one nine-ray census
same realize signature, hundreds of rays

the groundcover particle modifiers leave the depsgraph for the solve and for the hero kits, and go back **before a pixel is traced**. A 0.4 m clump was never an occluder at 12-46 m and `_cast_visible` already skipped hidden hits
the town had **no building layer at all**
outside the mill's own 670-line kit, all 999 `lm_` meshes rendered as flat gray massing. `hide_gray` had been hiding this at the pilot's 30 m radius; at `--region all` it correctly turns itself off
2,232 objects in the master; the dressing touched 555 instances and one corner

the blockout **already names every surface it paints** — `emb_mat_thatch`, `_plaster`, `_stone`, `_timber`, `_cobble` — exactly as the 21/29/15 crown recipes name a species. The dressing re-renders its MATERIAL CLASSES once. Heartlight, lamp glass, windows and water are excluded on stated rules
`masonry_scanned` could only fall back to **grey**
a missing role fell through to `masonry()`'s coursed procedural grey
with `roof_thatch` absent, every roof in Emberbrook would have become coursed stone — silently
`fb_mat` names the honest fallback per role; five CC0 roles were then intaken so none of them is needed
sections.note: Instruments: tools/emb_lum.py (the ruler), tools/dressing_texmeasure.py (the library's albedo ruler), macOS `sample` on the stalled process (the qsort and the realize), and the engine's own printed census.
